sources.citation: Beaumont, C. H. 1976. Austronesian languages: New Ireland. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study, vol. 2: Austronesian languages, 387-397. Pacific Linguistics C-39. (Same volume: Beaumont, 'History of Austronesian research: New Ireland', 4.2.8, p. 173; Capell's general chapter.)
sources.note: No remark on stress in any New Ireland language; Tangga is mentioned only for subgrouping, a quadral number, and a few sound correspondences. The volume's only 'Stress' section (no. 84, p. 475) is Lithgow's on Milne Bay languages, not Tangga.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2012. Change Request 2012-141 (submitted by John Brownie, SIL-PNG): split [tgg] Tangga into Fanamaket [bjp], Niwer Mil [hrc], Warwar Feni [hrw]; adopted 2013-01-23.
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic/lexicostatistic only. Cites its evidence as 'Lambrecht, Philip, Alison Kassell and Bonnie MacKenzie. 2005. Niwer Mil [tgg], Wawar Feni, and Fanamaket Survey Report. unpublished ms.'

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm D. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Nothing on Tangga stress; Tangga appears only as comparative lexical/grammatical data in ch. 8 (St George linkage). p. 261 names the descriptive sources: Maurer (1966) grammar and Bell (1977) dictionary.

sources.citation: Beaumont, C. H. 1972. New Ireland languages: a review. In Papers in Linguistics of Melanesia No. 3, 1-41. Pacific Linguistics A-35. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. Section 1.5.8 'Tangga' (p. 24) only records that Maurer's Grammatik der Tangga-Sprache was microfilmed in the Micro-Bibliotheca Anthropos series and is organised by parts of speech; 1.6.1.5 (p. 27) notes Maurer's 408-page dictionary and Bell's forthcoming dictionary being edited by Capell 'who is also giving it a grammatical introduction'. a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing.

tone.summary: Short orthography report; its Suprasegmentals section treats only stress (initial in most words). Tone, pitch and intonation are not mentioned at all.

sources.note: The survey behind the 2013 ISO split; SIL-PNG survey reports usually include wordlists and sometimes phonological notes per variety. SIL resource pages could not be reached by automated download to every download, so whether it was later released (SIL Electronic Survey Report) is unverified.
